citation: Tomczak, S. (2016). Polish Companies Bankruptcy. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5F600
evaluation: Five predeclared stratified grouped random holdouts. Each split uses validation for selection and early stopping, then refits final models on train plus validation before scoring the independent test partition. Means and standard deviations describe split variability, not confidence intervals.
evaluation_scope: The LSTM-GNN is evaluated as a one-snapshot inductive peer graph model. Its LSTM receives one observed vector, so this experiment does not test temporal modeling.
limitations: The supplied files contain no company identifiers or fiscal-year keys, so they cannot support longitudinal sequences, chronological splits, or company-clustered intervals.
Graph ablations test edge attention, unweighted edges, neighbor count, and relation channels; temporal persistence is not identifiable from this single-snapshot dataset.

When per-seed tuning is enabled, candidate selection uses only that split's validation partition; otherwise the supplied tuned config is reused. The selected models refit on train plus validation rows after selection. Earlier exploratory benchmark test records informed architecture development, so these results are not a confirmatory blinded evaluation. Seed variability is not a confidence interval and does not establish state-of-the-art performance.
